newsitem.title: PERU: Telefonica del Peru's $180 mln issue approved.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica del Peru's $180 mln issue approved.

text.p: Telefonica del Peru has received approval to issue over three years debt instruments with a maximum maturity of one year up to a total value of $180 million, a Lima Stock Exchange official said on Wednesday.

It is the first time the Lima Stocks and Securities Board (CONASEV) has given approval for a Peruvian company to issue short-term debt paper, the board's general manager, Victor Loyza, said in an interview.
The board also approved the issue of up to 50 million soles ($19.4 million) as the first tranche of the program, Loyza added.
The company has not announced the date of the first tranche's issue, but sources close to the operation said last month they hoped it would be in November.

The same sources added that the program's instruments will have a maturity of between 30 and 270 days and had already been classifed by Duff & Phelps del Peru with the local agency's second highest rating, DPp1.
The issue of the short-term paper "shows the development of our market," said Loyza. "We have no doubt other companies will follow suit."
Telefonica estimates it will invest $700 million this year as part of its three-year, $1.6 billion program that ends in 1998.
The company recently began a three-year corporate bond issue worth 250 million soles in the local market.
The firm is majority-owned by Spain's Telefonica de Espana after its $2.002 billion privatization in 1994.
